Los Angeles: Pacific Standard Time (PST) UTC-8; Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) UTC-7. Berlin: Central European Time (CET) UTC+1; Central European Summer Time (CEST) UTC+2.

During winter (standard time): PST (-8) vs CET (+1) difference = 9 hours. During summer: PDT (-7) vs CEST (+2) difference = 9 hours as well? Wait: -7 to +2 difference = 9 hours. So it's always 9 hours difference? Actually, check: In winter, Los Angeles is UTC-8, Berlin UTC+1 => difference 9 hours. In summer, Los Angeles UTC-7, Berlin UTC+2 => difference 9 hours. So indeed it's always 9 hours difference. But there might be a period when one is on DST and the other not? Let's check transitions: In US, DST starts second Sunday in March, ends first Sunday in November. In Europe, DST starts last Sunday in March, ends last Sunday in October. So there is a period from March to early March? Actually, from March 8 to March 14? Let's compute: In 2023, US DST started March 12, Europe DST started March 26. So between March 12 and March 26, Los Angeles is on DST (UTC-7), Berlin still on standard (UTC+1). That difference is 8 hours. After March 26, both on DST: difference 9 hours. Similarly, in fall: US DST ends November 5, Europe DST ends October 29. So between Oct 29 and Nov 5, Berlin is on DST (UTC+2), Los Angeles still on DST (UTC-7)? Wait, after Oct 29, Berlin goes back to standard (UTC+1). So between Oct 29 and Nov 5, Berlin is on standard (UTC+1), Los Angeles still on DST (UTC-7). That's 8 hours difference. After Nov 5, Los Angeles goes back to standard (UTC-8), Berlin standard (UTC+1) difference 9 hours. So there are periods where difference is 8 hours. So answer: Usually 9 hours, but during DST transition windows difference can be 8 hours.
